text:
anya: FYI — merged cust/turnstile/adapter-lora-v2 and pushed an int4 variant (q4f) to canary. Quick eval against billing-search quickpack shows notable embedding quality drop. Starting triage thread.

dev: Can you paste the eval summary and exact tag?

anya: Model tag: turnstile-adapter-v2-q4f (adapter merge -> bnb q4f quant). Eval command used: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite billing-search --model turnstile-adapter-v2-q4f --quickpack --batch 256 --cache on
```
Summary metrics: precision@10 0.62 (baseline int8: 0.83), ndcg@10 0.55 (baseline 0.77), avg_query_latency 32ms (baseline 50ms). Many queries have top-10 swaps.

mike: That's a big delta for retrieval. Any changes to tokenizer/preproc in the merge?

anya: No tokenizer changes; merge only added LoRA adapter weights. Quant config: 
```
quant_backend: bnb
quant_mode: q4f
adapter_only: true
per_layer_scaling: true
```
Tried with cache on/off, regression persists.

infra-bot: Canary route created: canary/turnstile -> turnstile-adapter-v2-q4f (cluster: canary-pool-3)

ci-bot: Regression ticket opened RG-2025-0412-02 (https://issues.redwood.ai/RG-2025-0412-02)

dev: My guess: bnb q4f per-layer scaling is distorting adapter projection space. Two quick experiments: 1) nf4 backend 2) q4f with per_layer_scaling=false. I'll run both and post the short results.

mike: Also add a run with `--quantizer-mode adapter-aware` (we added that flag to the quant pipeline last quarter) to see if adapter-aware placement helps.

dev: Running: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite billing-search --model turnstile-adapter-v2-q4f --quant-backend nf4 --adapter-only true --batch 256
```

dev: NF4 quick result: precision@10 0.78, ndcg@10 0.72, latency ~34ms. Much better but small gap to int8.

anya: Good recovery. How about per_layer_scaling toggles?

dev: q4f + per_layer_scaling=false -> P@10 0.80, NDCG@10 0.74, latency 33ms. q4f + adapter-aware-quantizer -> P@10 0.81, NDCG@10 0.75.

tara: Interesting — adapter-aware quantizer and disabling per-layer scaling both help. I'll run a layer-scan to localize sensitivity. Command: 
```
rwi-eval run --suite billing-search --model turnstile-adapter-v2-q4f --layer-scan true --quant-backend bnb --output /tmp/turnstile-layerscan.json
```

tara: Layer-scan summary: adapter projection layers 1-3 show the largest divergence after bnb-q4f. The low-rank adapter matmul ranges get heavy quantization noise when per-layer scales are applied in the current bnb implementation.

mike: Ops question: is the canary preprocess the same as prod? Infra?

infra-bot: Verified: canary-pool-3 uses same preprocess image and tokenizer bundle as prod; no transform differences logged.

anya: Given the customer-facing impact, proposal: 1) rollback canary to int8 adapter build 2) change default adapter quantizer in the CUST pipeline to nf4 or enable adapter-aware quantizer by default 3) add an embedding-drift unit test to the eval CI for future LoRA merges. Thoughts?

dev: +1. I'll prepare a small patch for the quant pipeline with a config flag `prefer_adapter_nf4=true` and add a gating unit test asserting P@10 drop < 0.03 vs int8 on the billing-search quickpack.

mike: I'll open the rollback deploy: `rwi-deploy promote --model turnstile-adapter-v2-int8 --route canary/turnstile --reason \"restore embed quality\"`

infra-bot: Deployment event: promoted turnstile-adapter-v2-int8 -> canary/turnstile (change id: DPL-9012)

ci-bot: RG-2025-0412-02 updated -> triaged (severity: high). Artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/evals/turnstile/1718456789-grid-results.json

tara: Follow-ups: I'll owner the bnb per-layer scaling investigation (math on scale placement + adapter hooks). Dev will own pipeline patch + tests. Mike will coordinate CS message and rollout timing.

anya: Thanks all. We'll hold customer traffic on canary until the patch and a quick smoke against billing-search pass. End of thread.
